title: Proth's criterion and the prime ladder reduction for ternary Goldbach up to 8.875 · 10^30
abstract: Lean 4 proofs, with no unproved steps, of two results from H. A. Helfgott and D. J. Platt, Numerical verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture up to 8.875 · 10^30, Experimental Mathematics 22, 2013, arXiv:1305.3062. First, Proth's criterion of Section 2, Theorem 2.3 in existential form; the converse printed after it, for every such a, is proved as converse but not compared: a Proth number N = k 2^n + 1 with 0 < k < 2^n is prime if and only if some integer a has Jacobi symbol -1 over N and a raised to the power N - 1 over 2 is -1 mod N. Second, Theorem 4.1, every odd number from 7 to T = 8875694145621773516800000000000 is a sum of three primes, derived from the two computations the paper rests on, which are explicit hypotheses and are not proved here: binary Goldbach for every even number from 4 to 4 · 10^18, the verification of Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi, and for each of the 492700 ranges of width 2^54 · 10^9 of Section 4 a ladder of odd primes with gaps at most 4 · 10^18 - 2 that starts within 2 · 10^18 above the left end point and ends less than 2 · 10^18 below the right end point, the paper's own computation. The entry does not verify any ladder or any binary Goldbach case, so it does not prove ternary Goldbach up to T; it proves that the paper's computations imply it. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem and binary Goldbach is open; neither is claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
